steps.title: Open the Dashboard
steps.narration: Let's start on the Dashboard — the first thing anyone sees when they open Trendora.
steps.point_out: A quiet green status strip just below the header confirms today's board is safe to trust — this is the same site-wide health check that now also watches for live-data drift.

steps.title: Discover the new live-data drift check
steps.narration: One click from anywhere opens the Data Manager, home to Trendora's data-integrity checks — including a brand-new one this update.
steps.point_out: A new "Live-vs-seed drift" card now sits right under "Storage footprint," with a plain-language sentence explaining exactly what it checks — no hovering or clicking required to read it.

expect.text: Byte/fixed-precision compares the last N dates a Fetch job returns against the committed seed.

steps.title: See the same check reflected site-wide
steps.narration: Head back to the Dashboard, and notice the top status strip already agrees with what the drift card just showed.
steps.point_out: The banner and the drift card read the exact same saved report — if a mismatch is ever found, this same strip turns amber everywhere in the app, not just on the Data Manager page.

steps.title: Confirm nothing else moved
steps.narration: Back on the Data Manager page, the rest of the page looks exactly as it always has.
steps.point_out: The "Rebuild snapshots for current universe" panel still renders normally right below the new card — the new check was slotted in without disturbing anything around it.

steps.title: Check the leaderboard is untouched
steps.narration: Let's swing by the Stocks leaderboard to make sure everything else in the app is unaffected.
steps.point_out: Ranked rows still carry their honest "Proven" / "Not yet proven" evidence badges next to each score, exactly as before.

steps.title: Check the evidence ledger is untouched
steps.narration: Finally, a quick look at the evidence ledger confirms it's exactly as it was.
steps.point_out: Every certified claim, including "leadership_score," still lists its real out-of-sample result — nothing about this page changed.
